reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about oxide formation, adhesion, passivation, and wear resistance in high-entropy alloys, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the synergistic behavior of such films under simultaneous wear and corrosion in HEAs, so specific support is needed.
premises: Targeted oxide-forming elements (e.g., Cr, Al) promote a mixed oxide layer on HEAs
The mixed oxide layer is robust and adherent under mechanical stress
The oxide layer passivates the surface, limiting corrosion
The adherent oxide layer provides a physical barrier against abrasive wear
The oxide layer synergistically mitigates both wear and corrosion simultaneously
